title: Compact clustered view and gesture-friendly column rails for large virtual tables
creator: Ayla Chen
description: Summary: Introduce a compact 'clustered' table density mode and a new gesture-friendly column-rail control to improve usability for very high-row-count views on touch and pointer devices. The clustered mode visually groups adjacent rows with small separators and semantic micro-headers to reduce perceived height while preserving scanability. The column rail is a narrow draggable affordance optimized for touch targets and momentum-aware resizing to avoid accidental full-width snaps. This ticket covers design tokens, component API surface, accessibility behavior, and handoff artifacts for engineering and PM.
background_and_motivation: Current compact modes compress row height but lose visual grouping, making long lists hard to scan when many rows share similar metadata.
Touch-initiated column resizing is brittle on mobile/tablet — users either miss the grab target or trigger accidental column snaps.
Engineering has requested a single, well-specified density token mapping and a small set of interaction patterns to implement across hosted and dedicated consoles to reduce divergence.

Goal: reduce vertical real-estate usage by ~30% in dense dashboards while improving discoverability of column resizing on touch and enabling fine-grained micro-adjustments without breaking virtualization measurements.
acceptance_criteria: Designs for clustered density mode (compact+grouping) with token mappings for spacing, font-size, and separator opacity
Prototype of gesture-friendly column rail with 44px min-touch target and momentum-aware delta smoothing
ARIA strategy defined: live region announcements on column-width change, focus behavior for keyboard and screen readers
Engineering implementation plan created with virtualization constraints and measurement strategy
Unit tests and visual regression spec added to design-system docs and storybook examples
Sign-off from Accessibility review and Product on usability trade-offs
design_notes: Clustered rows: introduce a subtle grouping separator token (token: surface.cluster-gap) that collapses repeated group metadata while keeping row skeletons predictable for virtualization measurements.
Micro-headers: optional inline header row for cluster boundaries (aria-hidden by default) to aid scanning without changing DOM semantics used by screen readers.
Column rail: 8px visible rail with 44px hit area centered on the rail; when user touches and drags, enter 'precision mode' where cursor delta is scaled by 0.3 for fine adjustments.
Momentum smoothing: 'inertia' only applied during continuous touch drag; sudden large deltas still allowed via modifier (Shift key) on desktop.
Snapping policy: default threshold-based snapping to preset widths is off in clustered mode; provide optional quick-snap affordance via double-tap on rail to cycle presets.
Density tokens: map existing density tokens (compact, comfortable, roomy) to clustered variants with explicit values for rowHeight, verticalPadding, token-space-y, and separatorOpacity.
Visual emphasis: use lower-contrast separators and a faint backdrop gradient on cluster starts to visually guide scanning without adding cognitive load.

Performance: maintain fixed rowHeight approach where possible; where variable row heights are required (multi-line content), provide a predictable 'expanded' state to avoid virtualization reflow thrashing.
engineering_tradeoffs_and_constraints: Virtualization relies on fixed heights for efficient scrolling. Clustered mode aims to keep rows fixed height; micro-headers are positioned absolutely to avoid DOM height changes.
Precision scaling for touch resizes requires a delta transform in the pointer handler; engineering flagged potential jitter on older tablets — recommend debounce+prediction layer.
Turning off snap-on-resize reduces some quick-layout UX but enables precise column proportions; provide keyboard shortcuts and double-tap quick-snap as compensations.
Accessibility: visible micro-headers should be aria-hidden; for screen readers, add programmatic grouping announcements via live-region when clusters enter viewport.
Telemetry: add resize interaction telemetry (duration, delta, precision-mode toggles) to help tune default smoothing values post-launch.
comments: 2025-11-04 — Ayla Chen: Initial sketches uploaded to Figma. Two variants: 'soft-cluster' (lighter separators) and 'dense-cluster' (more compression). Need engineering feasibility check on micro-header positioning.
2025-11-05 — Mateo Alvarez: Reviewed sketch. Asking Eng to validate virtualization constraints. Flagged potential problem with existing rowIndex->item mapping if we insert absolute micro-headers.

2025-11-06 — Priya Rao (Eng): Verified absolute-position micro-header approach is feasible; will add a small sentinel element per viewport to indicate cluster boundaries for accessibility without changing row heights.

2025-11-08 — Accessibility Review (Liam O'Connor): Micro-headers must be aria-hidden. Provide a live-region message when clusters are revealed via keyboard nav; confirm keyboard drag semantics (Space to pick up then Arrow to nudge) — listed in acceptance criteria.
2025-11-09 — PM (Ruth Delgado): Confirming product priority and asking to add telemetry metrics to measure number of times users use precision mode and double-tap quick-snap.
2025-11-11 — Design QA (Ayla): Added Storybook prototype and visual diff baseline. Noting a visual issue at 1200px where rail hit area overlaps column action buttons; will iterate on spacing token.
2025-11-12 — Mateo: Merging final spec into handoff doc. Engineering to pick up in next sprint; estimate 2-week dev cycle including unit tests and accessibility tweaks.
risks: Older browsers/tablets may surface jitter during touch precision mode; mitigation: add configurable smoothing and disable precision on underpowered devices.
Changing row visuals could break downstream plugin dashboards that rely on explicit DOM structure; plan: add feature-flag and migration notes in design-system changelog.
Telemetry adds privacy surface; ensure events do not contain row-level PII and are covered by telemetry policy.

Eng to prototype rail interaction in a playground and validate on iPad (due 2025-11-20)
Accessibility to sign off on keyboard and screen-reader flows (target 2025-11-18)
